function.name: create_a_docker_file
function.description: This function generates a Dockerfile in the specified directory with basic configuration. The Dockerfile will be tailored to a simple Python application. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Dockerfile will be created. It should be a valid directory path relative to the current working directory.

base_image.description: The base image to use for the Dockerfile, representing the starting point for the build.

maintainer.description: The name of the maintainer or author of the Dockerfile.

expose_port.description: The port number that the container should expose. This is typically the port that the application listens on.

entrypoint.description: The command that will be executed when the Docker container starts.

function.name: create_kubernetes_yaml_file
function.description: Generates a Kubernetes deployment and service YAML file in the specified repository directory. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

directory_name.description: The name of the directory where the Kubernetes YAML file will be created. This should be the root directory of the repository.

deployment_name.description: The name of the deployment to be created. This should be a unique identifier for the deployment.

image_name.description: The name of the Docker image to be used in the deployment. Include the image version tag if necessary.

replicas.description: The number of replicated pods desired in the deployment.

port.description: The port number that the container exposes for communication.

service_type.description: The type of Kubernetes service to be created for the deployment.

message.content:
Below is a complete “starter kit” you can drop into the **nodejs‑welcome** repository.  
It contains:

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `Dockerfile` | Builds a lightweight Node.js image. |
| `k8s.yaml` | Deployment + Service for Kubernetes. |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | GitHub Actions workflow that builds & pushes the image on every push to `main`. |

> **NOTE** – The repository already contains a `package.json`, `app.js`, etc.  
> If you want to keep the existing `Dockerfile` (if any) you can replace it with the one below.

---

## 1. Dockerfile

```dockerfile
# Use the official Node.js 18 Alpine image
FROM node:18-alpine

# Create app directory
WORKDIR /app

# Copy package files first to leverage Docker cache
COPY package*.json ./

# Install production dependencies
RUN npm ci --only=production

# Copy the rest of the source code
COPY . .

# Expose the port the app listens on
EXPOSE 3000

# Start the application
CMD ["node", "app.js"]
```

> *If your app listens on a different port, change `EXPOSE 3000` and the `containerPort` in the Kubernetes YAML accordingly.*

---

## 2. Kubernetes YAML (`k8s.yaml`)

```yaml
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-deployment
spec:
  replicas: 2
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: nodejs-welcome
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: nodejs-welcome
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: nodejs-welcome
        image: <YOUR_DOCKERHUB_USERNAME>/nodejs-welcome:latest
        ports:
        - containerPort: 3000
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: nodejs-welcome-service
spec:
  type: LoadBalancer   # Change to NodePort or ClusterIP if you prefer
  selector:
    app: nodejs-welcome
  ports:
  - protocol: TCP
    port: 80          # External port
    targetPort: 3000  # Container port
```

> Replace `<YOUR_DOCKERHUB_USERNAME>` with your Docker Hub account name.  
> If you’re deploying to a cluster that doesn’t support `LoadBalancer`, switch to `NodePort` or `ClusterIP`.

---

## 3. GitHub Actions Workflow (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)

```yaml
name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [ main ]

jobs:
  build:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

    steps:
    - uses: actions/checkout@v3

    - name: Set up Node.js
      uses: actions/setup-node@v3
      with:
        node-version: '18'

    - name: Install dependencies
      run: npm ci

    - name: Run tests
      run: npm test

    - name: Log in to Docker Hub
      uses: docker/login-action@v2
      with:
        username: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}
        password: ${{ secrets.DOCKER_PASSWORD }}

    - name: Build Docker image
      run: |
        docker build -t ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }} .

    - name: Push Docker image
      run: |
        docker push ${{ secrets.DOCKER_USERNAME }}/nodejs-welcome:${{ github.sha }}
```

> **Secrets required in the repository settings**  
> * `DOCKER_USERNAME` – Your Docker Hub username.  
> * `DOCKER_PASSWORD` – Your Docker Hub password or personal access token.

---

## 4. Add, Commit & Push

```bash
# From the root of the repository
git add Dockerfile k8s.yaml .github/workflows/ci.yml
git commit -m "Add Dockerfile, Kubernetes YAML, and GitHub Actions workflow"
git push origin main
```

That’s it! Once pushed, the GitHub Actions workflow will automatically run on every push to `main`, building the Docker image, running tests, and pushing the image to Docker Hub. The Kubernetes YAML can be applied with `kubectl apply -f k8s.yaml` once you have a cluster ready.
